findings.title: Zero-length date/time vector elements pass bound, decode to minDate with nil error
findings.claim: Zero-length date/time elements pass the new bound and still allocate one Go value per claimed element, decoding to minDate with a nil error instead of being rejected.

findings.title: Dimension bound counts wire bytes but allocation is sized in Go bytes (~16-24x amplification)
findings.claim: The bound compares Dimensions against len(data)/elemMin (wire bytes) while reflect.MakeSlice allocates using the Go element size, so a peer can still trigger allocation far larger than the payload (e.g. ~4GiB from a 256MiB body for vector<text,N>).

findings.title: Recursive per-element size floor's overflow-saturation branch has no test coverage
findings.claim: The saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize guarding against a nested peer-controlled Dimensions overflow is never exercised by any test, so a bug in the comparison, boundary, or int64-to-int narrowing there would go uncaught.

findings.title: PR body overstates how many new tests fail against pristine code (3 of 7 pass unchanged)
findings.claim: The PR body's claim that every new test fails against pristine code is wrong for 3 of 7 test functions: two pass unchanged against base as regression guards, and one doesn't even compile against base.

findings.title: Oversized VInt element length narrows to -1, silently decoding as an empty value
findings.claim: With the one-byte floor letting variable-length vectors through, a max-width VInt element length converts via int(m) to -1, so no payload bytes are consumed and the element silently decodes as an empty string with a nil error; pre-existing, deferred as issue #1106.

findings.title: Nested vector element type does not decode into interface{} (deferred #1085)
findings.claim: Nested vector support for interface{} destinations is deferred; the PR only turns the crash into an error rather than fully supporting nested vector decoding into interface{}.

findings.title: Surplus trailing bytes in a generic vector payload are still silently accepted (deferred #1086)
findings.claim: Surplus trailing bytes in a generic (non-float-fast-path) vector payload are still accepted rather than rejected, unlike the float fast paths which reject the same malformed payload; left as-is and out of scope.

findings.title: Companion change rejecting dim<1 in metadata parsers (#1093) is not part of this PR
findings.claim: The companion change (#1093) rejecting dim < 1 in metadata parsers is not in this tree; the variable-length finding shapes are well-formed with dim>=1 and are not covered by it.

findings.title: Dimension-bound error message omits the element type unlike the fast-path errors it preempts
findings.claim: The new dimension-bound error omits info.SubType, unlike the fast-path errors it preempts; validator judged this an unsupported wording preference rather than a defect since the message still names the operation and both peer-controlled numbers.

findings.title: New bound rejects driver's own zero-byte marshaled payloads that no server would ever return
findings.claim: The new bound rejects every payload marshalVector produces for a fixed-size element encoded in zero bytes (nil pointers, zero time.Time, UnsetValue), flipping from silent zero-filled decode to an error, but Cassandra's FixedLengthSerializer would reject such a write server-side so the read can never occur in practice.

findings.title: marshalVector emits a wire-invalid vector value instead of erroring when an element under-marshals
findings.claim: marshalVector writes bytes with no prefix and no length check when an element (nil pointer, UnsetValue, or zero time.Time) marshals to fewer bytes than vectorFixedElemSize, producing a wire-invalid value the caller only learns about via the server's InvalidRequest; pre-existing, not touched by this diff.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize(nil) panics on a caller-constructed VectorType with nil SubType
findings.claim: With Dimensions > 0 and non-nil data, a caller-constructed VectorType with a nil SubType reaches vectorFixedElemSize(nil) and panics calling Type() on a nil interface; pre-existing since the pre-diff fast-path switch sat behind an identical guard.

findings.title: Peer-controlled type descriptor text (up to 65535 bytes) reaches error messages verbatim (CWE-117)
findings.claim: The new error at marshal.go:1048 formats the peer's type descriptor with %v, and NativeType.String prints the raw custom name the server sent verbatim, up to 65535 bytes including newlines/escape sequences, reaching an error applications routinely log; not filed since the driver already prints info this way elsewhere.

findings.title: Malformed VectorType name parsing can panic on unguarded slice/index operations
findings.claim: frame.go does spec[1:len(spec)-1] and spec[:idx] where idx may be -1, and helpers.go:264 indexes names[1] unguarded; a malformed name from the wire panics there. Pre-existing and unchanged; reviewer could not rule out a string that survives frame-time parsing but panics in the Scan-goroutine parser.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recursion depth is capped well below stack-overflow risk
findings.claim: Recursion in vectorElemMinSize follows peer type-descriptor nesting, but the descriptor is capped at 65535 bytes and each level costs ~43 characters, capping depth near 1500, far below a Go stack overflow; checked and not a finding.

findings.title: Nested-vector 'no Go type' error cannot name the element type, only prints the bare custom prefix
findings.claim: For a nested vector, the new guard prints the bare prefix 'no Go type for element type custom(...)' because getCassandraLongType builds the nested VectorType's NativeType from a constant prefix rather than the parsed spec, so the PR's goal of naming what the server sent doesn't work for nested vectors; held back because a consumer might rely on the bare-prefix value.

findings.title: Callsite completeness for changed getCassandraLongType output was verified only by manual grep
findings.claim: Every non-test reader of the TypeInfo returned by the changed getCassandraLongType was traced by hand since the repo has no symbol-aware search; a consumer reached through an interface or reflection, or comparing TypeInfo by equality, would not appear in that trace.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType fallback change is broader than stated intent, affecting non-vector nested types too
findings.claim: The basic-type fallback in getCassandraLongType is not scoped to vector elements: it also changes Custom()/String() for any unrecognized type resolved recursively through list, set, map, tuple, and UDT definitions, a wider change to exported TypeInfo output than the PR description states.

findings.title: Unmarshal's doc comment has never documented vector decoding, including the new error conditions
findings.claim: Unmarshal's doc comment has no 'vector' row in the CQL-to-Go table and VectorType's own comment covers only Zero(); this pre-existing gap now sits under two new error conditions the PR adds.

findings.title: No release-notes/changelog channel exists for communicating this decode-behaviour change
findings.claim: The repository removed upstream's CHANGELOG.md and neither README.md nor CONTRIBUTING.md states a SemVer or breaking-change policy despite go.mod tagging v1.x.y releases, so there's no channel through which this decode-behavior change reaches a consumer pinning a released tag.

findings.title: Test helper makeVectorType builds a TypeText descriptor for a wire name the real parser maps to TypeVarchar
findings.claim: makeVectorType(TypeText, "UTF8Type", dim), used for every vector<text,...> test case, sets typ=TypeText for a wire name that getApacheCassandraType actually maps to TypeVarchar; harmless today but a future divergence wouldn't be caught by these tests.

findings.title: No measurable performance regression from the new unconditional per-row vectorElemMinSize call
findings.claim: unmarshalVector now calls vectorElemMinSize(info.SubType) unconditionally ahead of the float fast paths and recomputes it every row uncached; benchmarks across dims 128-1536 show head and base indistinguishable within noise with 0 allocs/op on both.

findings.title: No test for the headline behavior change: empty non-NULL payload now errors instead of decoding silently
findings.claim: No test pins that unmarshalVector(vector<int,3>, []byte{}, &dst) changed from nil error with a zero-filled slice on base to an explicit 'do not fit' error on head; existing tests use a 2-byte payload or Dimensions==0, neither covering this case.

findings.title: Accepted behaviour change is tested only for vector<int,3>, not the other fixed-size types it also affects
findings.claim: The new bound also flips decoding for nil-pointer element slices of every fixed-size type and for zero time.Time / UnsetValue cases, but no table test round-trips Marshal then Unmarshal over those shapes to pin the new verdict deliberately.

findings.title: No test covers a variable-length element type whose real minimum wire size exceeds the 1-byte floor
findings.claim: No test uses vector<smallint,N> or vector<duration,N> to confirm the bound stays permissive enough to accept a real, well-formed server payload for such types.

findings.title: No test confirms the new bound leaves the float fast-path error message unaffected for longer-than-minimum payloads
findings.claim: No test asserts that a vector<double,3> payload of 32 bytes still produces 'expected 24 bytes, got 32' rather than the new bound's message, the boundary where the message substitution stops applying.

findings.title: Allocation-bound test only covers nested fixed-size shapes, not variable-length elements
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures peak allocation only for the nested fixed-size shape; there's no allocation assertion for a variable-length element type (vector<text,N> into []string or any), where the 1-byte floor permits the largest Go-side allocation.

findings.title: No test covers a zero-dimension inner vector as an element type, the fallback path in vectorElemMinSize
findings.claim: No test covers vector<vector<float,0>,N>, the shape reaching the 'return 1' fallback; TestVectorElemMinSize pins the floor value but nothing pins what unmarshalVector then allocates for it.

findings.title: No test exercises the real Scan path end-to-end for the new dimension-bound rejections
findings.claim: Every new dimension-bound and no-Go-type test calls unmarshalVector or Unmarshal directly; none exercises iterScanner.Scan -> scanColumn -> Unmarshal to pin that a hostile payload's error surfaces cleanly to a Scan caller with no panic in the intermediate plumbing.

findings.title: No test drives the new bound through a type nested three or more vector levels deep
findings.claim: No test confirms the recursion terminates with a sane floor for a type nested three-plus vector levels deep; described as minor since Dimensions is bounded before depth could matter in practice.

findings.title: 'No Go type' test for nested vector into interface{} asserts only a substring, not the rendered identifier
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsAnElementTypeWithNoGoType/nested_vector_into_an_interface asserts only that the error contains 'no Go type for element type', not what identifier follows, so a regression in the rendered identifier would go unnoticed.

findings.title: No unit test exercises getCassandraLongType's basic-type fallback outside the vector path
findings.claim: No test covers a List<UnknownType>, an unknown map value, or a UDT field to confirm the widened Custom()/String() population behaves correctly for those positions, since the same function backs all of them.

findings.title: Benchmarks cover only flat vector<float,N>, not nested or variable-length-element vectors
findings.claim: There is no benchmark for a nested vector or a variable-length element vector, both of which now exercise the recursive prologue on every value, so a future regression in that recursion would not show up.
